cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Fair Means I Can Win
cards.instruction: Agree to any rule or bargain only after interpreting fairness in a way that preserves your advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took a rose off the cake when you took one. Now cut us equal slices.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was plastic. I was removing the decorations. You ate an icing rose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the top. Equal slices after preparation is only fair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then your slice comes from the bare patch. Mine can have the remaining icing rose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal means matching decoration. Cut the last rose in half before I agree to the slices.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 eaten icing prompts A3 exclusion of preparation; B4 bare-patch allocation makes A5 demand half the remaining rose.

relationship.evidence: B4 offers a concrete offset for the already-eaten icing instead of moralizing.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts equality only if it gets still more icing despite B4 compensating allocation.

specificity.evidence: A1 two roses and B2 plastic/edible contrast make the error clear; B4 remaining edible rose supplies exact quantity.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 split-before-agreement is a concise enactment of conditional fairness.
